description: Thermal protection relay (ANSI 23, 26, 38, 45, 49, 74, 77, 94) with four temperature sensors, alarm, shutdown, fault and ventilation relays, analog output and Modbus RTU
source: Electron do Brasil, Mapa de Registradores MODBUS RTU, Relé de Proteção Térmica EP4 IoT

sources.title: Mapa de Registradores MODBUS RTU, Relé de Proteção Térmica EP4 IoT
sources.note: linked in issue #129; the document linked for the EP3 in issue #128 has the same text

notes: All registers are holding registers. The document numbers them 1 to 99 and calls the type Holding Register (40.000), so the addresses are 1-based (address on the wire = number minus 1). The document does not say so explicitly: if a read fails, try address_base 0.

The document allows 2400 to 57600 bps with automatic baud rate detection, 8 data bits and 1 stop bit. It gives no parity, default baud rate or slave address: 9600 N and 1 are placeholders; the slave address is in register 50.
Temperatures are shown in the document with one decimal and a scale of -1000:10, which it does not explain. They are given as raw values: check against the display before applying a scale.

Registers 26, 42, 43, 45, 46, 47, 48, 49 and 61 are bit fields, one entry per bit. The command bits are write-only. Registers 80 to 83 (map latitude, two registers each, both labelled latitude) and the maximum current-output temperature of sensor 4 are not in the document or not clear, so they are left out.
The EP3 IoT document linked in issue #128 has exactly the same content and title (EP4 IoT), so this map may not match an EP3 IoT.
Written from the manufacturer's document; not tested on a device.
